messages.author: 07419993cc085236
messages.subject: INLA behavior with categorical variable
parts:
Hi, 

I am having some issues with fitting a model with one (or several) categorical variables in a logistic regression model. My understanding based on looking at a number of examples was that INLA would fit factors relative to one of the levels. I am not getting that behavior - I get a fit to each level separately and I can't figure out why this is happening and more importantly how to interpret the values I am reading. 

For a quick example, this is how a toy model is specified (the actual model has a random effect and a bunch of other fixed effects): 

formula <- Y ~ -1 + intercept + TESTFAC 

result_mod <- inla(formula_mod,
                       family = "binomial",
                       data = data_run_inla,
                       Ntrials = N_rep,
                       control.fixed = list(mean = 0, prec = 1/100),
                       verbose = TRUE,
                       keep = FALSE, debug = TRUE)

summary(result_mod) returns this: 
 
Fixed effects:
                mean     sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant    mode kld
intercept     0.6565 5.7735   -10.6789   0.6563    11.9824  0.6565   0
TESTFACGREEN  0.8114 5.7735   -10.5239   0.8112    12.1373  0.8114   0
TESTFACRED   -0.1549 5.7735   -11.4903  -0.1551    11.1710 -0.1549   0

Just so it's clear, the "TESTFAC" variable is indeed a factor and has only 2 levels: 
 > class(data_run_inla$TESTFAC)
[1] "factor"
> levels(data_run_inla$TESTFAC)
[1] "GREEN" "RED"  

In addition, the data doesn't have NAs, and the 'Y' variable is specified properly to use Ntrials. 

Any insight on this would be much appreciated! 
Thanks, 
Romain

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA behavior with categorical variable
parts:
The default behavior is as with lm(). 
I guess the -1 makes it not recognize the confounding with the ‘intercept’

There is another expand strategy , see the FAQ, which force the behavior you observe

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA behavior with categorical variable
parts:
Hi,

“factors” is one of the R problem children. ;)

With ~ 1 + myfactor, model.matrix can detect the redundancy in the model and by default eliminates a factor level. It could in theory do that with
~ -1 + intercept + myfactor
as well, if intercept was a covariate with all ones, but the more complex model definition setup in inla doesn’t try to guess as much as model.matrix what model you wanted to have.

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA behavior with categorical variable
parts:
For full control, use a suitable model.matrix call to construct the
Indicator dummy variables that you wanted the factor to produce.
You can then use that matrix directly I the model, if you supply data as a list instead of data.frame. Since you had an explicit intercept term I suspect you may be using inla.stack? In that case, inla.stack has support for such matrices, and nsport them though the process correctly.

Finn

messages.author: 07419993cc085236
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA behavior with categorical variable
parts:
Actually my specification of explicit intercept was a legacy from some old that I didn't think was needed to update - as I didn't exactly expect it to have aparticular effect. 

It turns out that simplifying the intercept specification to 

formula <- Y ~ 1 + TESTFAC   

 works perfectly well in my case. 

Thanks for the help! 
Romain
